faq.q: Why does a calculator use binary?
faq.a: Its circuits are made of switches that are either on or off, so it is easiest to store numbers using only two digits, 1 and 0. Seven is written 0111 and five is 0101.
asks: How does a calculator store numbers?

faq.q: How do logic gates add numbers?
faq.a: An adder circuit adds two binary digits and any carry from the column before, using XOR gates for the sum and AND and OR gates for the carry, just like column addition on paper.

faq.q: How does a calculator display the answer?
faq.a: It turns the binary result back into decimal digits and lights the right segments of each digit on its screen. Seven segments are enough to show any digit from 0 to 9.

faq.q: How fast does a calculator add?
faq.a: The adding itself takes far less than a millionth of a second. Almost all the time is spent waiting for you to press the keys.
Multiplying is built from adding and shifting digits, just as long multiplication on paper is. Doubling a binary number is simply shifting every digit one place to the left.
asks: Does a calculator multiply by adding?

facts: Seven in binary is 0111 and twelve is 1100.
